Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed. As we work toward signature we reviewed the MSA + Order Form and legal pushed back on a few SLA items. Attached is our redline (Strata_SLA_Redlines_030228.docx). The main items are: 

- Uptime target: ask is 99.95% for the Production API rather than the 99.9% in your draft.
- Service credits: they want a formula tied to monthly invoice and a floor/ceiling we don't yet see in your docs.

Can you share Redwood's position on these? If needed our procurement counsel is available next week for a quick call with legal.

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Strata's redlines. High level thoughts below; please weigh in so I can give them a consolidated response by EOD.

Quick read summary (my POV):
- Uptime: 99.95 is materially higher; we can consider conditional 99.95 for "mission-critical" endpoints/instances with capacity/commitments, otherwise we should hold at 99.9.
- Credits: we should keep a cap (e.g., monthly invoice or 50% of monthly invoice) and a cure period; unlimited credits is a non-starter.
- Response times: 15-min P1 ack is fine if they accept that remediation SLA depends on incident classification and can be mitigated by auto-fallback to alternate region/model.
- Maintenance: 2-hour hard weekly window + 14-day notice is restrictive for infra upgrades; propose rolling maintenance language (max 4 hours per month with per-instance stagger and 7-day notice for critical patches).

Asks:
1) Ben — can you confirm ops feasibility of a 2-hour weekly freeze vs rolling maintenance? Any risk to KV cache invalidation or batch throughput?
2) Marissa — want to own commercial tradeoffs (credit cap, fee for 99.95), and set expectations for procurement/legal call next week.

I attached a short Redwood position doc (Redwood_SLA_Response_030228.pdf) with suggested language to start with. I plan to propose a call Mon/Tue.

Thanks,
Tessa

Quick ops note after reviewing Strata's redlines and our suggested language:

- Uptime 99.95: achievable for single-tenant/dedicated pools where we can reserve capacity; for shared-hosted models achieving consistent 99.95 globally is risky without dedicated capacity. Suggest we make the 99.95 conditional on dedicated capacity + maintenance blackout windows.
- Maintenance windows: a hard 2-hour weekly window will significantly constrain our patching cadence. Alternative: allow a maximum of 4 hours/month per customer for planned disruptive maintenance, with the ability to stagger across instances (so the global service isn't down). Require 7-day notice for routine maintenance and 14-day notice for major upgrades; call out emergency maintenance carve-outs.
- Credits: ops prefers a formula tied to incident root cause (platform vs customer misconfig). We should propose credit only for platform-level downtime and exclude incidents caused by customer-managed integrations.

I've attached an ops note with suggested text snips (ops-maintenance-note.txt). Happy to jump on the call next week.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Support & Reliability, Redwood Inference

David / Strata team — thanks for the patience while we reviewed your proposed redlines. We've consolidated commercial, legal, and ops feedback and attached a single counter-proposal (Redwood_SLA_Counter_030306.docx). Summary of our position: 

- Uptime: We can offer 99.95% for Production API if Strata takes Dedicated Capacity or a committed throughput tier (we will specify eligible endpoints in the Order Form). Otherwise the default for shared-hosted is 99.9%.
- Credits: We propose a capped credit formula equal to up to 100% of the monthly invoice for qualifying platform outages; credits are prorated and exclude customer-caused incidents.
- Response/ack times: We accept 15-min P1 acknowledgement for customers on 24/7 support plans (additional support fee applies); remediation SLAs will be defined by incident classification and subject to reasonable diagnostics cooperation.
- Maintenance: Compromise language — routine maintenance: maximum 4 hours/month (can be scheduled as weekly 1-hour windows or a single 4-hour window) with 7-day notice; major upgrades 14-day notice; emergency maintenance as required with post-event RCA.

Next steps: 
1) Please review the attached counter and confirm whether Strata can accept the Dedicated Capacity premium for 99.95, or whether you prefer to stay on shared-hosted with 99.9.
2) If the counter is acceptable, Marissa will issue a revised Order Form with pricing and I'll share a DocuSign link for execution.

Proposed call times to finalize commercial: Wed 03/07 10:00-10:30 PT or Thu 03/08 09:00-09:30 PT — please let us know which works.

Thanks again — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
